outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The State of Mathematical Reasoning in Open-Source LLMs
outline.description: This chapter contextualizes the research by reviewing the current limitations of open-source language models in mathematical reasoning, contrasting them with closed-source benchmarks, and introducing the core problems this paper addresses.
subtopics: The evolution of LLMs in quantitative reasoning
The gap between proprietary models (GPT-4, Gemini) and open-source alternatives
Key challenges in mathematical reasoning (complexity, structure, memory)
Limitations of existing pre-training data sources (arXiv vs. web),
Introducing DeepSeekMath: The proposed solution and key contributions

outline.description: A detailed technical deep-dive into the creation of the DeepSeekMath Corpus from Common Crawl, covering the iterative data selection pipeline, classification techniques, quality validation against existing datasets, and decontamination strategies.
subtopics: The problem of dataset bias and data scarcity in math training
Seed corpus initialization and negative example selection
Domain-level analysis for domain-specific enrichment (e.g., MathOverflow)
Benchmark decontamination strategies to ensure fair evaluation
Comparative analysis against MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2
Multilingual capabilities: The advantage of non-English mathematical data

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Pre-training Strategy and Base Model Optimization
outline.description: This chapter explains the architectural decisions behind DeepSeekMath-Base 7B, specifically the rationale for initializing with a code-trained model, the token distribution strategy, and ablation studies comparing different data sources.
subtopics: Why initialize with a Code-trained model (DeepSeek-Coder)?
